served.stem: According to the passage, many ectomycorrhizal fungi can reach nitrogen held in dead tissue because they
choices: release enzymes that break down protein in leaf litter
capture nitrogen from air trapped inside the root mantle
take up ammonium faster than a root hair can take it up
move nitrogen along the hypha as chains of polyphosphate
trade nitrogen with arbuscular fungi on neighbouring roots
served.bankWhy: Paragraph 6 draws the line between the two association types right here: ectomycorrhizal fungi secrete enzymes that break down protein in litter, while arbuscular fungi lean on nitrogen already freed into the soil.

proof.quote: secrete enzymes that break down protein in leaf litter

passage.title: The Trade Beneath the Forest Floor

distractorNotes: Paragraph 6 never mentions nitrogen being taken from air, and no part of the passage describes nitrogen fixation.
Paragraph 6 does say nitrogen moves as ammonium, but that is the form it travels in, not the reason litter nitrogen becomes available.
Polyphosphate is how paragraph 6 says phosphate travels, and swapping it onto nitrogen is a one word change.
No exchange between the two fungal types appears anywhere in the passage, so this is outside its scope.

answer.text: release enzymes that break down protein in leaf litter
answer.line: Paragraph 6, sentence 3: many ectomycorrhizal fungi secrete enzymes that break down protein in leaf litter, freeing nitrogen locked in dead tissue.

steps: Find ectomycorrhizal next to nitrogen: paragraph 6, sentence 3.
Read the means in the same sentence. Enzymes do the unlocking: they break down protein in leaf litter.
Note the contrast that follows. Arbuscular fungi rely on nitrogen already freed into the soil.
